**Direct answer: No.** Idempotency keys make retries safe only inside a bounded window, and only if you resend the same parameters. Both Stripe and AWS say the server's memory of a key is limited. After that window, a retry may run the operation again.

**Stripe**
- Stripe API v1 may remove keys once they are at least 24 hours old. If you reuse a key after that, Stripe treats it as a new request. This is Stripe's one explicit time limit. The docs say Stripe "can" prune keys at 24 hours, not that it does so at exactly that point.
  https://docs.stripe.com/api/idempotent_requests
- Keys can be up to 255 characters. Stripe suggests V4 UUIDs or another high-entropy random string.
  https://docs.stripe.com/api/idempotent_requests
- If the parameters differ from the original request, Stripe returns an error.
  https://docs.stripe.com/api/idempotent_requests
- In v1, Stripe saves the status code and body of the first request once the endpoint begins executing. Retries with that key return the saved response, including `500` errors.
  https://docs.stripe.com/api/idempotent_requests
- In v1, Stripe does not save a result if the request fails validation or conflicts with a concurrent request, so those requests can be retried.
  https://docs.stripe.com/api/idempotent_requests
- In v1, only `POST` requests take idempotency keys. `GET` and `DELETE` are idempotent by definition, and a key has no effect on them.
  https://docs.stripe.com/api/idempotent_requests
- API v2 behaves differently. Retries don't repeat successful operations, and Stripe retries failed or partial work to completion where possible. I read only the summary of this on the v1 page, not the v2 page.
  https://docs.stripe.com/api/idempotent_requests

**AWS**
- AWS's Builders' Library says retaining knowledge of a request indefinitely is impractical. It also says an old identifier could collide with a much later request.
  https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/making-retries-safe-with-idempotent-APIs/
- For EC2 instances, the Builders' Library limits retention to the resource's lifetime plus an interval. It gives no number.
  https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/making-retries-safe-with-idempotent-APIs/
- ECS `RunTask` has a client-token TTL of 24 hours, or the resource lifetime plus one hour, whichever is lower. So the window can be shorter than 24 hours.
  https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/APIReference/ECS_Idempotency.html
- ECS says not to reuse a client token for different requests.
  https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/APIReference/ECS_Idempotency.html
- ECS token length limits are 36 ASCII characters for `CreateService` and `CreateTaskSet`, and 64 for `RunTask`.
  https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/APIReference/ECS_Idempotency.html
- EC2 tokens are case-sensitive strings of up to 64 ASCII characters.
  https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ec2/latest/devguide/ec2-api-idempotency.html
- EC2 idempotency is scoped to a Region, or to an Availability Zone for some requests. The same token can launch resources in a different Region or zone.
  https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ec2/latest/devguide/ec2-api-idempotency.html
- EC2 returns `IdempotentParameterMismatch` if a token is reused with different parameters (other than Region or Availability Zone). ECS returns `ConflictException` for the same case.
  https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ec2/latest/devguide/ec2-api-idempotency.html and https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/APIReference/ECS_Idempotency.html
- Only some EC2 actions use client tokens. A few are idempotent by default, and the rest have no such guarantee.
  https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ec2/latest/devguide/ec2-api-idempotency.html
- AWS says to retry `5xx` errors with backoff and not to retry `4xx` errors.
  https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ec2/latest/devguide/ec2-api-idempotency.html
- A retry of a completed AWS request returns a "semantically equivalent" response, not necessarily an identical one. The EC2 page says the result "might contain updated information, such as the current creation status."
  https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/making-retries-safe-with-idempotent-APIs/ and https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ec2/latest/devguide/ec2-api-idempotency.html

**Comparison**
- Stripe documents a fixed 24-hour pruning rule for v1. AWS has no single universal limit. The window depends on the service, and the Builders' Library ties it to the resource's lifetime. ECS `RunTask` is the one number I confirmed, and I did not find a specific retention figure for EC2.
- Both vendors detect parameter mismatches. Both also say that outside the retention window, the server can't be relied on to deduplicate.

**What the evidence doesn't establish**
- I did not verify retention periods for other AWS services. A search snippet mentioned 10 minutes for DynamoDB and 5 minutes for some others, but I didn't confirm either on an AWS page.
- I did not read Stripe's v2 idempotency page or its "retry idempotent requests" page.

Sources:
- https://docs.stripe.com/api/idempotent_requests
- https://aws.amazon.com/builders-library/making-retries-safe-with-idempotent-APIs/
- https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/APIReference/ECS_Idempotency.html
- https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ec2/latest/devguide/ec2-api-idempotency.html
